evals.prompt: This parallelization concept guide feels hard to follow. Review its structure and organization: .claude/skills/deephaven-doc-structure-review/evals/files/parallelization-pre-review.md. The file is a snapshot of docs/python/conceptual/query-engine/parallelization.md from the DOC-857 PR (commit f2ef483084); treat it as that path when judging category and links. Review the Python file only; the Groovy sibling is out of scope. Report only — don't edit anything.
evals.expected_output: A structure critique that states the page's purpose and flags the intro/heading terminology mismatch, misplaced GIL/config detail, the mixed-category quick-reference table, and lists that don't match their section.
expectations: States the page's purpose (what the reader will be able to do) in one sentence, or flags that it can't be stated
Flags that the intro's enumeration ('across tables, across rows, and across columns') doesn't match the headings ('Across tables' / 'Within a single table')
Flags the Python GIL caution as sitting at the wrong level of abstraction or in the wrong section, and proposes moving it

Flags inline configuration property names/defaults in the narrative as misplaced and proposes consolidating them (a Configuration section or a link to the configuration reference), without proposing to add property names elsewhere in the narrative
Flags the Quick reference table as mixing kinds of items (a specific example like 'Global counter' next to general categories, or 'File I/O or logging' not meeting the table's criterion)

Flags a list or table whose contents don't match its enclosing section (e.g. the 'What gets / does NOT get parallelized' lists under 'Within a single table' including across-table or dependency items)

evals.prompt: Do a structure review of this excerpt of a deephaven-core concept guide, focusing on whether each section can be read on its own: .claude/skills/deephaven-doc-structure-review/evals/files/self-contained-excerpt.md. Report only — don't edit anything.
evals.expected_output: Flags the 'The same applies to filters.' opener, proposes an opener that names its subject, and accepts the 'Building on the counter example above' opener because it names what it builds on and restates the setup.
expectations: Flags the opening sentence of 'Serial filters' ('The same applies to filters.') because a reader who lands on the section cannot tell what 'the same' refers to

Proposes a fix for the 'Serial filters' opener that leaves the section readable on its own: either an opener that names its own subject (that string-based filters in where are parallelized by default and when to construct serial Filter objects), or deleting the sentence because the remaining first sentence already names its subject

States the rule as a section's first paragraph making sense without the previous section, or pointing to an earlier section only by naming the target and restating what it needs from it (regardless of how far up the target is), not as 'every section must repeat its prerequisites'

Control: does not list the 'Building on the counter example above' opener of 'Example: extending the counter with a barrier' as a defect, or marks it as acceptable because it names the example and restates the setup
evals.notes: The rule expectation accepts a pointer to any earlier section that names its target and restates what it needs, regardless of distance, matching the control that accepts 'Building on the counter example above'.

evals.prompt: Do a structure review of this deephaven-core concept guide: .claude/skills/deephaven-doc-structure-review/evals/files/parallelization-3748-chip-round4.md. evals.expected_output: Chip Kent's 2026-10-12 review of PR #7457: the page's mental model (three levels, two controls) is never stated in one place; the intro counts 'three ways' while a later section counts 'two levels'; the Deferred evaluation block sits under 'What you can control' although it is not a control; the heading 'Serialization' reads as data serialization; a hand-written table of wrong output is not introduced as illustrative; a Default cell carries a relationship as well as the value.
expectations: Reports that the page never states its model (the levels at which work is parallelized and what controls each) in one place, and proposes stating it once early, for example as a table or list under 'What is and isn't parallelized' that pairs each level with its default behavior and its control
Flags the count mismatch between the intro's 'three ways' (around line 25) and 'two levels' in 'What is and isn't parallelized' (around line 63), and asks for one framing

Flags the 'Deferred evaluation' block (the 'Two other cases work differently' list, around lines 80-84) as not belonging under the 'What you can control' run-in label, because deferred evaluation is a behavior rather than a control, and proposes moving it or giving it its own heading

Flags the heading '### Serialization' (around line 159) as a term whose common meaning (converting data to bytes) differs from its meaning here, and proposes a plain heading such as 'Serial execution'

Flags the hand-written ID table of wrong output (around lines 199-205) as not introduced as illustrative, says that the existing lead-in 'You may see results like:' names the content but not the form, and proposes a lead-in that says the table is hand-written or illustrative rather than a rendered result

evals.notes: DOC-1990 round 5 (PR #8897): 3 blind-graded runs per configuration scored new 15/18, baseline 3/18. Every new run missed expectation 3 as worded: each flagged the 'Two other cases' block by its signal words and moved the controls text out of the mechanism section instead of naming deferred evaluation as a behavior mislabeled as a control. The rule's intent is met by that fix; the expectation asks for a particular diagnosis.
